chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated from Muḥammad ibn Jazk, who said:

I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام: I own camels, and I have caretakers over them, and I do not go out with them except on the road to Makkah due to my desire for hajj, or only rarely to some places. So what is obligatory upon me, when I go out with them, to do? Is shortening required in salat and breaking the sawm during travel, or completion?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “If you are not constantly bound to them, and you do not go out with them on every journey except to Makkah, then upon you is shortening and breaking the fast.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel that carries legal consequences for worship
key_terms.جِمَالًا: camels owned for transport or livelihood
key_terms.قُوَّامٌ: caretakers or attendants managing the animals

ai.seo_question: Does a person who only occasionally travels with his camels to Makkah shorten prayer and break the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the prayer and fasting of a person who owns transport animals but does not regularly travel with them as a professional occupation. Since his journeys are occasional and not habitual, especially being mainly for hajj, he must shorten his salat and break his fast while traveling.
